intro: The trade deadline is six days out and the Colts are already selling, with Josh Downs asking out after Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner left town. The Ravens will start an undrafted rookie on Thursday night, and the Chargers sit at 0-7 with no touchdown in 27 drives. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Josh Downs asks out as the Colts' sell-off grows
top.dek: The Colts receiver requested a trade, ESPN reported, and did not deny it. Indianapolis has already sent Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner to NFC West teams. Downs is on an expiring rookie deal with the deadline set for Nov. 10.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Ravens turn to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano with Lamar Jackson out
top.dek: Jackson had thumb surgery and Tyler Huntley is out with turf toe, so Fagnano starts Thursday night against Jacksonville. Kicker Tyler Loop also went on injured reserve with a groin injury.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Alex Singleton leads the NFL with 101 tackles
top.dek: The Broncos linebacker has the most tackles in the league through eight games. Denver is 6-2 and visits Carolina on Sunday, and the Panthers' own preview names Singleton as the anchor of the defense.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 27: Chargers drives since their last touchdown
top.dek: Los Angeles kept offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel through the bye, then lost 24-9 to the Rams and fell to 0-7. The Chargers ran for 2.6 yards per carry in the loss.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Bengals and Falcons meet Sunday morning in Madrid
top.dek: Cincinnati is 5-2 and Atlanta is 3-5, with kickoff at 9:30 AM ET on NFL Network. It is the Bengals' third international game. Watch how Atlanta uses pass rusher James Pearce Jr. in his return.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Allen ties a 1950 mark as Bills hold the AFC top seed

stories.text: Allen runs his way into a 76-year-old quarterback record
stories.summary: Josh Allen scored on a 1-yard run to finish the opening drive against Baltimore. That gave him nine rushing touchdowns through seven games, which ties Johnny Lujack's 1950 mark for a quarterback. He also threw two touchdown passes in the 36-10 win that moved Buffalo to 6-1.

stories.text: DJ Moore is back from his shoulder injury, Palmer limps off
stories.summary: Moore returned after missing the previous two games with a shoulder injury. His 49-yard catch set up a James Cook touchdown. Josh Palmer left the game limping after a deep incompletion, and the game coverage gave no update on his status.

stories.text: Kincaid leads the Bills with 86 yards and a touchdown
stories.summary: Dalton Kincaid caught four passes for 86 yards and a score against Baltimore. Allen finished 21 of 34 for 289 yards with two touchdown passes, and the Bills rushed for 146 yards as a team.

stories.text: 87: penalty yards on 10 Bills flags in a sloppy win
stories.summary: Buffalo drew 10 penalties for 87 yards against the Ravens. The first half also included questionable play calls from head coach Joe Brady. The Bills still won by 26, but Monday night in Minnesota leaves less room for that kind of sloppiness.

stories.text: At Minnesota on Monday night: best offense meets best defense
stories.summary: Buffalo visits the Vikings on Monday, Nov. 9 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Minnesota's defense leads the league in points allowed, and the Bills have the league's highest-scoring offense. The Vikings are coming off their first loss of the season.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Miami wins the first half and still loses to New England

stories.text: Dolphins' defense dominates early, then the lead disappears
stories.summary: Miami led New England 13-3 at halftime and fell to 1-6 after losing 24-19. The defense held the Patriots to 1-for-5 on third down in the first half. Josh Uche had a sack on third down, and Jacob Rodriguez forced a fumble that Juju Brents recovered. Miami pressured Drake Maye on 57.1 percent of his first-half dropbacks while sending one blitz.

stories.text: Proctor needs to clear protocol before Sunday
stories.summary: Rookie guard Kadyn Proctor suffered a concussion against the Jets in Week 7. He showed symptoms after that game and went into the protocol. Jeff Hafley said Monday that Proctor is still in protocol and gave no word on Week 9. Jarrett Kingston started in his place against New England, his first start in three years.

stories.text: Willis lives on third down in a losing effort
stories.summary: Malik Willis went 21 of 32 for 211 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against New England. He was 7 of 10 on third down for 54 yards and a score. His 1-yard touchdown pass to Malik Washington put Miami ahead late in the first half.

stories.text: 33%: Miami's rushing success rate against New England
stories.summary: Ollie Gordon carried 19 times for 69 yards, and the Dolphins ran successfully on only one of every three attempts. That left Willis to carry the offense while facing pressure on 45 percent of his dropbacks. Miami will need a steadier ground game to stay on schedule against Detroit.

stories.text: Lions (5-2) visit Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Miami hosts Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Lions come in at 5-2 with recent wins over Minnesota and Green Bay. The Dolphins are 1-6 and still have to settle their offensive line after Proctor's concussion.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Halftime line change helps Maye take over in Miami

stories.text: A halftime line change flips the offense in Miami
stories.summary: New England trailed 13-3 at the break, then moved Ben Brown in for Walter Rouse at left guard. Maye's pressure rate dropped from 57.1 percent in the first half to 38.5 percent in the second. He went 9 of 10 for 146 yards and three total touchdowns after halftime, with a 158.3 passer rating.

stories.text: Henry's foot is the question as Hollins nears a return
stories.summary: Hunter Henry left the Miami game before halftime with a foot injury. Mike Vrabel said Monday he had no expectations yet and wants to see how Henry responds this week. Mack Hollins and Reggie Gilliam can come off injured reserve, and Vrabel said they could potentially return against Green Bay. A.J. Brown, who hurt his knee in practice before the Miami game, could be back at practice.

stories.text: Kyle Williams keeps catching touchdowns long
stories.summary: All five of Kyle Williams' career touchdown catches have gone for at least 30 yards. Maye threw two touchdown passes of 30-plus yards at Miami and has done it in three games this season. Williams gives the offense a deep target while the receiver room stays banged up.

stories.text: -7: New England's turnover margin ranks 31st
stories.summary: The Patriots own the eighth-ranked offense at 367.3 yards a game and the ninth-ranked scoring defense at 20.3 points allowed. Their turnover differential of minus 7 ranks 31st in the league. Green Bay sits at plus 4, tied for seventh, so ball security decides this one.

stories.text: Packers visit Gillette on Sunday at 4:25 p.m.
stories.summary: New England hosts Green Bay on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. Both teams are 5-3. A win would make the Patriots 4-0 at home, their best home start since 2019. Green Bay's pass offense ranks second in the league, while its run game ranks last.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Hall set to return as Jets try to stop a slide

stories.text: Jets move the ball all day and still lose to Las Vegas
stories.summary: New York gained 424 yards and scored on its first six possessions against the Raiders. It led 23-14 at halftime and still lost 38-33 to fall to 2-6. The Raiders won after trailing at the break for the first time in 13 games, and the defense gave up three touchdown passes to Kirk Cousins.

stories.text: Breece Hall expected back; Bailey and Ossai questionable
stories.summary: Breece Hall has missed five games with a quad injury and is expected to return against Kansas City. Edge David Bailey missed his first NFL game with a groin injury and is listed as questionable. Offensive tackle Max Mitchell is in concussion protocol and Joseph Ossai has an ankle injury, and both are also questionable.

stories.text: Adonai Mitchell turns seven catches into 142 yards
stories.summary: Adonai Mitchell caught five passes for 78 yards and a touchdown in the first half against Las Vegas. He finished with seven catches for 142 yards. Garrett Wilson opened the game with a 31-yard catch on the first play.

stories.text: 424: yards for the Jets, and no win to show for it
stories.summary: The Jets turned 424 yards into 33 points and settled for field goals on some trips. Jason Sanders kicked at least four of them. The game ended when Jeremy Chinn intercepted a Jets pass from the 35-yard line.

stories.text: At Kansas City on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: The Jets visit the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Kansas City is 5-2 and has lost two straight. New York has dropped three in a row.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Undrafted rookie Fagnano starts for Ravens

stories.text: Ravens give undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano the start
stories.summary: Coach Jesse Minter named Fagnano the starter for Thursday night. The 25-year-old from UConn went 10 of 21 for 91 yards against Buffalo, with an interception and a lost fumble, after Lamar Jackson hurt his thumb on the first snap. Tyler Huntley's turf toe leaves Baltimore no other choice.

stories.text: Loop lands on IR, Moody expected to kick
stories.summary: Kicker Tyler Loop went on injured reserve Tuesday with a groin injury, and Jake Moody is expected to handle the kicking. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins missed practice with a knee issue. Fagnano worked through an ankle injury, then practiced fully Tuesday in a brace, and the Ravens signed Kedon Slovis from the Packers' practice squad as a backup.

stories.text: Henry grinds, but the runs are not breaking
stories.summary: Derrick Henry has 156 rushing yards on 45 carries during Baltimore's three-game skid. That works out to 3.5 yards a carry. The Ravens need more from their lead back with a rookie quarterback under center.

stories.text: 3: second-half points in three straight Ravens losses
stories.summary: Baltimore has scored a combined three points after halftime during its three-game losing streak. The latest was a 36-10 loss at Buffalo. The offense now turns to a first-time starter.

stories.text: Thursday night vs. 5-2 Jaguars on Prime Video
stories.summary: Baltimore hosts Jacksonville Thursday at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video. The Jaguars (5-2) beat Indianapolis 42-7 last week, hold a +7 turnover margin and allow a league-best 77.4 rushing yards a game. Expect Henry to face the toughest run defense in the league.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals fly to Madrid on a three-game win streak

stories.text: Bengals leave early for Madrid, call it a six-day week
stories.summary: Cincinnati flew out Tuesday after practice, took Wednesday off and will practice Thursday and Friday at Spain's national team facility. That is two days earlier than the 2019 London trip. Coach Zac Taylor said he treats the week like a six-day week, and Dexter Lawrence said a win would tie Pittsburgh atop the AFC North before the Nov. 15 rematch.

stories.text: Cornerback DJ Turner questionable with a heel injury
stories.summary: Turner is listed as questionable for the week with a heel injury, per the AP. Rookie edge Cashius Howell had wrist surgery and is expected to go on injured reserve.

stories.text: Burrow joins Manning, Wilson and Stafford in a rare club
stories.summary: Joe Burrow is the fourth quarterback in NFL history with at least four touchdown passes and a passer rating of 115 or higher in three straight games. Peyton Manning (2004), Russell Wilson (2020) and Matthew Stafford (2025) did it before him. The Bengals have won three in a row and sit at 5-2, their best start since 2021.

stories.text: 27: points Bengals have allowed on opening drives
stories.summary: Cincinnati has given up three touchdowns and two field goals on opponents' first possessions, tied for the fourth most in the league. Opponents have scored on their first drive in five of seven games, and in three straight. The fix has to come before Atlanta gets the ball first.

stories.text: Sunday morning in Madrid against Atlanta
stories.summary: Cincinnati plays the Falcons (3-5) Sunday at 9:30 AM ET on NFL Network. It is the Bengals' third international game, after a 27-27 tie with Washington and a 24-10 loss to the Rams, both in London. Mike Gesicki brings the NFL's longest active touchdown streak at five games.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns must stop the run before New Orleans

stories.text: Browns run defense gets gashed again by Pittsburgh
stories.summary: The Steelers ran for 200 yards and three touchdowns at 6.1 a carry. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger took the blame for missed tackles, and Todd Monken said the group must be better against the run. Cleveland also gave up 141 rushing yards the week before.

stories.text: Schwesinger plays through a sprained ankle
stories.summary: Schwesinger has played on a sprained ankle since the Oct. 11 loss to the Jets and has not missed time. Monken said it is a different ankle than the one reported. Cornerback Tyson Campbell returned Sunday after a second-quarter neck injury and a concussion evaluation.

stories.text: Szmyt kept Cleveland on the board
stories.summary: Kicker Andre Szmyt hit field goals of 32 and 49 yards, the Browns' only points against Pittsburgh. He is 16 of 18 on the season with three game-winning kicks. Cleveland needs touchdowns, but Szmyt has been steady.

stories.text: 117: rushing yards allowed in the first quarter alone
stories.summary: Cleveland gave up 117 net rushing yards in the opening quarter, including a 51-yard run by Jaylen Warren. The Browns managed 34 rushing yards themselves and converted 4 of 13 third downs. Watson was sacked eight times for 41 yards.

stories.text: Sunday at 2-5 Saints, 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cleveland visits New Orleans at the Superdome, its third straight road game after Tennessee and Pittsburgh. The Saints are 2-5 and coming off a bye, and they ran 17 times for 18 yards in a 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh in Paris. Reuters reported the Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, though the team site still listed him at last check.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers use the bye to fix the red zone

stories.text: Red zone play-calling is the bye week project
stories.summary: Pittsburgh scored touchdowns on three of five trips inside the Browns' 20. Two others ended in field goals after pass calls on first and second down inside the 15. D.K. Metcalf has eight drops, second most in the NFL, per Steelers Wire.

stories.text: Pittman and Wilson remain out heading into the bye
stories.summary: Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson are both out right now. A return soon after the bye would help a receiver group that totaled 43 yards against Cleveland. Metcalf had 4 of them.

stories.text: T.J. Watt owns the Browns, 20.5 sacks and counting
stories.summary: Watt had two sacks Sunday, which gives him 20.5 career sacks against Cleveland, the most any player in NFL history has against the Browns. Cameron Heyward and Patrick Queen each had 1.5 sacks. Watt called the bye well-timed.

stories.text: 18.0: points per game allowed, fourth in the NFL
stories.summary: The Steelers defense also ranks sixth in yards allowed and third against the run, per ClutchPoints. Watt has 7.5 sacks and 9.5 tackles for loss. The article says Pittsburgh must still prove itself against the Bills, Patriots, Jaguars, Broncos and Chiefs.

stories.text: Bye in Week 9, then Sunday night at Cincinnati
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is off this week and next plays at the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 8:20 PM ET on NBC. Cincinnati will have played in Madrid by then. The winner takes control of the AFC North race.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans return from the bye aiming at tackling, penalties

stories.text: Ryans resets the Texans around tackling and penalties
stories.summary: DeMeco Ryans spent the first post-bye press conference on fundamentals instead of the opponent. Houston will drill wrapping up and finishing tackles, and the coaches want fewer holding calls on the edge after several long runs came back. Ryans also wants the offense to stop running only out of its jumbo package and to mix in more passing looks.

stories.text: Ryans has no new word on players hurt before the bye
stories.summary: Asked about the players who were banged up going into the open week, Ryans said there was no significant update and that the staff would track progress through the week. Receiver Jaylin Noel is on injured reserve, and Ryans said the team will miss his big plays and his work on returns. Houston's Week 9 practice reports were not out yet.

stories.text: Tank Dell is back, and Houston hopes he stretches the field
stories.summary: Dell played his first regular-season game since December 2024 against the Giants and caught one pass for 43 yards. He sat out all of 2025 with a knee injury and went onto the 53-man roster before Week 7. The argument is that his speed from the slot and in motion can pull coverage off Nico Collins.

stories.text: 1: C.J. Stroud has thrown one interception in 247 attempts
stories.summary: Through seven games Stroud has completed 160 of 247 passes for 1,867 yards and 11 touchdowns, with a 100.7 passer rating. He has also taken 15 sacks. The Texans sit at plus 3 in turnover margin, while the Chargers are at minus 6.

stories.text: Texans visit the 0-7 Chargers Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Houston plays at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8, against the league's only winless team. The Chargers' offense has gone 27 straight drives without a touchdown, and Justin Herbert has thrown 10 interceptions. Houston has a chance to turn the bye into a reset.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Downs wants out as Colts face a Nov. 10 deadline

stories.text: Josh Downs asks out as the Colts' sell-off continues
stories.summary: Receiver Josh Downs requested a trade, reported by ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, and did not deny it. He said he is open to whatever happens. Indianapolis already sent guard Quenton Nelson and tackle DeForest Buckner to NFC West teams. Downs, 25, is on an expiring rookie deal and had 26 catches for 307 yards through seven games before he scored last Sunday.

stories.text: No new injuries reported, but Taylor left early Sunday
stories.summary: Indianapolis has not reported new injuries from the 42-7 loss in Jacksonville. Jonathan Taylor left the game early in the fourth quarter, and the account of the game gave no reason. Daniel Jones, who tore his Achilles last season, is on track to start Sunday.

stories.text: Rookie CJ Allen makes 10 tackles in his first start
stories.summary: Linebacker CJ Allen started against Jacksonville and finished with 10 tackles, a sack and a tackle for loss. Training camp injuries slowed his start to the season. With the Colts giving young players more snaps, he is one of the few bright spots.

stories.text: -11: Colts have the NFL's worst turnover margin
stories.summary: Indianapolis has 15 giveaways, nine interceptions and six lost fumbles, against only four takeaways. The offense has scored fewer points each week lately: 22, 20, 10, then 7. The last win came 30-13 at Washington on Oct. 4.

stories.text: Colts host the Cowboys Sunday at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Indianapolis hosts Dallas at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8, with Adam Amin and Drew Brees on the call. The Cowboys lead the all-time regular-season series 11-6. Watch whether Jones holds the job through four quarters.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars hit the road on a short week against a rookie QB

stories.text: Ravens turn to an undrafted rookie to face the Jaguars
stories.summary: Baltimore will start Joe Fagnano on Thursday. Lamar Jackson hurt his right thumb on the first snap against Buffalo and needs surgery, and Tyler Huntley has a turf toe injury. Fagnano, 25 and out of UConn, went 10 of 21 for 91 yards with an interception in relief last week. Jacksonville arrives at 5-2.

stories.text: Tuten sits out with ribs as the short week starts
stories.summary: Running back Bhayshul Tuten did not practice Tuesday with a rib injury. Guard Ezra Cleveland (knee and ankle) and safety Antonio Johnson (ankle) were limited. Linebacker Branson Combs (shoulder) and lineman DaVon Hamilton, who is already out for the year, did not practice.

stories.text: Lawrence throws three touchdowns before an early exit
stories.summary: Trevor Lawrence completed 10 of 14 passes for 210 yards and three touchdowns against Indianapolis before the blowout let him leave the game. Jacksonville also ran for a season-best 183 yards. Lawrence now takes a short week to Baltimore.

stories.text: 72.2: rushing yards per game the Jaguars allowed through Week 7
stories.summary: Jacksonville held opponents to 72.2 rushing yards per game and 3.2 yards per carry through Week 7, the best marks in the league at that point. Against Indianapolis the defense added four sacks and three takeaways. That run defense now faces a Ravens offense starting a rookie quarterback.

stories.text: Jaguars visit the Ravens Thursday at 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video
stories.summary: Jacksonville plays at M&T Bank Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 5, on Prime Video. Baltimore has a rookie starting at quarterback and several injury questions of its own. Jacksonville then travels to Nashville to face the Titans on Nov. 15.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans use the bye to fix third downs and penalties

stories.text: Titans' bye list starts with third downs and red zone
stories.summary: Cincinnati converted 7 of 10 third downs and scored touchdowns on five of six red-zone trips in the 43-36 overtime win. Tennessee also took 10 penalties, including holds on three kickoff returns. After the Jeffery Simmons trade, the Titans hold four first-round picks over the next two drafts.

stories.text: Rookie receiver Carnell Tate nurses a shoulder injury
stories.summary: Tate missed the loss in Cincinnati with a shoulder injury and did not practice that week. Through seven games he has 34 catches for 413 yards and one touchdown. The bye gives him extra time before the Titans host Jacksonville on Nov. 15.

stories.text: Tony Pollard runs for 117 yards and two scores in a loss
stories.summary: Pollard carried the ground game in the 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals, with 117 yards and two touchdowns. Cam Ward threw for 304 yards and two touchdowns in the same game, his first 300-yard day. Tennessee still lost.

stories.text: 6: one-score losses for the 1-7 Titans
stories.summary: Tennessee has dropped six games by one score. The defense has given up close to 1,000 yards over its last two games. The Titans have also lost twice despite outrushing the opponent, posting a better passer rating and winning the turnover battle.

stories.text: Bye in Week 9, then Jacksonville comes to Nashville
stories.summary: Tennessee is off this week. The next game is Sunday, Nov. 15, at home against the Jaguars at 1 PM ET on Fox. The Titans enter it at 1-7.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Payton hits 200 as Broncos retake the West

stories.text: Payton gets win No. 200 as Denver retakes the AFC West lead
stories.summary: Denver beat Kansas City 28-24 to move to 6-2 and give Sean Payton his 200th career win. The offense sputtered for three quarters, then the defense closed it out. Malcolm Roach and Jonathan Cooper teamed up on the sack that ended the game.

stories.text: Two starting safeties are hurt as Denver turns to Carolina
stories.summary: Brandon Jones played through a questionable tag, then left with a hamstring injury and sat out the second half. Talanoa Hufanga missed a second straight game with an ankle injury after not practicing all week, and one report has him out multiple weeks. Receiver Jaylen Waddle played through a chest injury.

stories.text: Alex Singleton leads the NFL in tackles
stories.summary: The linebacker has 101 tackles through eight games, the most in the league. Carolina's own preview points to him as the anchor of a defense that ranks 11th in scoring at 20.6 points per game. Opponents have scored on 48 percent of their red zone trips against Denver.

stories.text: 740: Bo Nix's second-half passing yards this season
stories.summary: Nix has thrown for 740 yards and seven touchdowns after halftime this year, with one interception. His winning drive against Kansas City was the fifth of the season, tied for the most among quarterbacks. Pro Football Talk counts 15 in his career, the most by any quarterback through three NFL seasons.

stories.text: Broncos visit Carolina on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver goes to Charlotte for the first time since 2022 against a 3-4 Panthers team that has lost two straight and is 0-4 on the road. Nix has averaged 7.3 yards per attempt over his last two games, up from 5.5 in the first six. Carolina will use interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash for the first time. The Broncos then have their Week 10 bye and host Las Vegas on Nov. 22.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs stopped at the goal line, then a flag

stories.text: A false start wipes out Rice's last-second touchdown
stories.summary: Kansas City led by 11 with under nine minutes left, then lost 28-24 as Denver scored on two straight drives. On the final possession the Chiefs reached the 1-yard line, and a fourth-down touchdown to Rashee Rice at the final whistle was called back for a false start. Mahomes was sacked on the last play and called the division race a dogfight.

stories.text: Delane and Woods are the names to track at defense
stories.summary: Cornerback Mansoor Delane was inactive with a shoulder injury after missing practice Thursday and Friday. Defensive tackle Peter Woods left the Denver game early and was ruled out. Rashee Rice returned after two missed games, and Patrick Mahomes (knee) and Travis Kelce (ankle) played without designations.

stories.text: Rookie Emmett Johnson turns a screen look into 128 yards
stories.summary: The fifth-round running back caught five passes for 128 yards and his first NFL touchdown, a 73-yard score on third and 10 against a Denver zero blitz. He added a 38-yard catch on the next possession and a 44-yard kickoff return with under two minutes left. Denver expected him to stay in and block, and he slipped out into the route instead.

stories.text: 9: pass-catchers Mahomes found in the loss
stories.summary: Mahomes threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns, and the targets spread across nine different receivers. Noah Gray caught a 4-yard score late in the third quarter, and Johnson added the long touchdown. The passing game produced points. Penalties and the end of the game did the damage.

stories.text: Jets visit Arrowhead on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City hosts a Jets team that is 2-6 and has lost three straight. New York ran for 166 yards against Las Vegas last week, with Braelon Allen gaining 147, so the Chiefs run defense gets an early test. Kansas City then travels to Atlanta in Week 10.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: A 95-yard kick return sparks Raiders' comeback

stories.text: Dylan Laube's 95-yard kickoff return flips the Jets game
stories.summary: Laube took the kickoff back for a touchdown seconds after the Jets went ahead. It was the first kickoff return score in the NFL this season and the first for the Raiders since 2011. Jeremy Chinn then intercepted a pass in the end zone with 14 seconds left to protect the 38-33 win.

stories.text: Cornerback Darien Porter's groin keeps Raiders thin on the back end
stories.summary: Porter hurt his groin on the Jets' first offensive play and did not return, and the team has not given a timeline. Jermod McCoy is expected to take on a bigger role. Brock Bowers played through a calf issue after practicing in full, and Carter Runyon (foot) is on injured reserve with his 21-day window open.

stories.text: Rookie Mike Washington Jr. carries the load with 25 rushes
stories.summary: Washington ran 25 times for 83 yards as the Raiders rushed 33 times against 26 pass attempts. The balance helped Kirk Cousins, who went 19 of 26 for 247 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions.

stories.text: 2: Ashton Jeanty's carries in a 38-point win
stories.summary: Jeanty carried twice for 9 yards but caught three passes for 64 yards on four targets. A 45-yard screen gain set up the go-ahead drive. Cousins and Bowers, who had seven catches for 92 yards and two scores, did most of the damage.

stories.text: Raiders visit the 49ers on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Las Vegas plays at Levi's Stadium against a 49ers team that is 6-1 and coming off its first loss. The Fox broadcast is regional, so check local listings. The Raiders return home to face Seattle in Week 10 and visit Denver on Nov. 22.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers stick with McDaniel at 0-7

stories.text: Chargers keep Mike McDaniel despite a stalled offense
stories.summary: The Chargers did not fire their offensive coordinator during the bye and lost 24-9 to the Rams. The offense has not scored a touchdown in its last 27 drives and ran for 2.6 yards per carry. Los Angeles led 9-3 on two field goals before the Rams scored before halftime.

stories.text: Cornerbacks Jackson and Shelley sit out with hamstring injuries
stories.summary: Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley were both inactive against the Rams after limited practices. Deane Leonard (concussion) and Kayode Awosika (fibula) were also out. David Njoku is nearing a return from injured reserve, and Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris played.

stories.text: Practice squad call-up Isas Waxter makes his presence felt
stories.summary: Waxter, elevated because of three cornerback injuries, made two tackles for loss against Puka Nacua. Tuli Tuipulotu added his third sack of the year, and rookie Akheem Mesidor pressured Matthew Stafford often. The defense held the Rams to 10 yards on five first-half carries before fading late.

stories.text: 10: Justin Herbert's interceptions through seven games
stories.summary: Herbert threw two interceptions against the Rams. Los Angeles ran for only 64 yards and did not reach the end zone. Herbert said he wants to play better and make better decisions.

stories.text: Texans visit SoFi on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Houston is 2-5 and arrives with its own struggles. The Chargers lead the all-time series 6-4, and the teams split the last two meetings. Last year's Week 17 game at SoFi was low scoring, with Herbert leading two second-half touchdown drives.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Jones backs Schottenheimer as Dallas heads to Indy

stories.text: Jones rules out a coaching change after the Arizona collapse
stories.summary: Owner Jerry Jones said he sees no repeat of the 2010 Wade Phillips firing, even after Dallas lost 33-30 in overtime to Arizona. The Cowboys are 3-5 and have held a winning record in only one of 25 weeks under Brian Schottenheimer. Jones said many people let his coach down, and Dak Prescott pushed back on putting the loss on one person.

stories.text: Downs and Locke sit in the concussion protocol
stories.summary: Safeties Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke are both in the concussion protocol, and Locke's status for Indianapolis is uncertain. Downs has a full week to finish the five-step return process. Tight end Jake Ferguson had clean tests on his ankle and has a chance to play, while Luke Schoonmaker missed Week 8 with a groin injury.

stories.text: Prescott ranks fifth in the NFL with 2,046 passing yards
stories.summary: Dak Prescott has 14 touchdown passes, ninth in the league, against five interceptions. He has not thrown one in the last two games. Dallas scores 27.4 points a game and allows 26.6.

stories.text: 15: straight games Dallas has allowed 20 or more points
stories.summary: That is the longest active streak in the league. Arizona scored touchdowns on all three of its fourth-quarter drives and gained 222 yards in the quarter. The Cowboys have scored 30 or more in five games and still sit at 3-5 because they keep giving up leads.

stories.text: Cowboys visit the 2-6 Colts Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Dallas plays at Lucas Oil Stadium. Indianapolis has lost four straight, including a 42-7 loss at Jacksonville. Both defenses rank in the league's bottom six in points allowed.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants try to end a 13-game skid in Philly

stories.text: Giants carry a 13-game losing streak into Philadelphia
stories.summary: New York has lost 13 straight in Philadelphia, a streak that dates to October 2013. The Giants lead the NFC East at 4-2-1 after a clean win in Houston with no turnovers and four penalties. They go back on the road Sunday as the division leader.

stories.text: Skattebo is day to day with a hamstring problem
stories.summary: Cam Skattebo worked with trainers on the sideline at the first practice after the bye, and John Harbaugh called him day to day. The hamstring bothered him after a 42-yard overtime run in Houston. With Tyrone Tracy Jr. on injured reserve, Devin Singletary and Gregory Desrosiers are the other healthy backs, and the team signed Eric Gray to the practice squad.

stories.text: McCarthy goes 20 of 28 for 252 in his first start
stories.summary: J.J. McCarthy posted a 99.1 passer rating in the win at Houston. The offense turned the ball over zero times and rushed for 188 yards, a season high. Harbaugh had named him the starter over Jameis Winston.

stories.text: 24: points New Orleans led by before McCarthy's rally
stories.summary: McCarthy entered in the fourth quarter, threw for 243 yards and led three scoring drives. The Giants still lost 34-27. Harbaugh made him the starter about three weeks after New York sent Minnesota a fifth-round pick for him.

stories.text: Giants visit the Eagles Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: New York then hosts Washington on Thursday night, Nov. 12, on Prime Video. The Giants will watch Skattebo's hamstring all week behind a thin backfield. Philadelphia has lost six in a row.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles stick with Sirianni as the skid hits six

stories.text: Sirianni says no coaching changes after sixth straight loss
stories.summary: Nick Sirianni said Monday he will not change his staff after the 27-10 loss to Washington, and he defended offensive line coach Chris Kuper. The Eagles are 2-6, their longest skid since 2012. They are 5-11 over their last 16 games, going back to last season.

stories.text: Barkley plays through a back injury
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley played only 10 snaps against Dallas because of the back injury. He missed practice Wednesday and Thursday, was limited Friday and was set to play Sunday night. ESPN also reported the Eagles will not trade him before the Nov. 10 deadline.

stories.text: McKee goes down five times in the loss to Washington
stories.summary: Tanner McKee took five sacks, the most the Commanders have recorded this season. Charles Omenihu had one sack and three quarterback hits, and Odafe Oweh beat Jordan Mailata off the edge late for another.

stories.text: 5.2: yards per carry Washington gained on the Eagles
stories.summary: Dallas and Washington both ran well against Philadelphia's front the last two weeks. The Giants arrive with Skattebo, who ran for 124 yards and a touchdown in Houston.

stories.text: Eagles host the Giants Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The trade deadline falls Nov. 10, two days after the game. Philadelphia then takes its Week 10 bye and returns Nov. 22 against Pittsburgh. A win would end the six-game skid before the break.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders thin out up front before the Rams

stories.text: Payne's season-ending injury guts the tackle group
stories.summary: Daron Payne reportedly suffered a season-ending Jones fracture in Friday's practice and joined Javon Kinlaw on injured reserve. Both will miss at least four games. Tim Settle Jr. and Shy Tuttle are the healthy tackles left, and Jer'Zhan Newton must be activated before he can play.

stories.text: McNichols lands on IR with a midfoot injury
stories.summary: Jeremy McNichols hurt his foot Sunday and should miss significant time. He had just come back from five weeks on injured reserve with a quad injury. Washington claimed Robert Henry Jr. off waivers from Seattle, and Devin Neal and Craig Reynolds are practice squad options.

stories.text: Omenihu hits Philadelphia's offense all night
stories.summary: Charles Omenihu had a sack, three quarterback hits and a fumble recovery in the 27-10 win. The defense sacked Tanner McKee five times, its season high, without Payne, Kinlaw or Newton. Odafe Oweh added a late sack.

stories.text: 3: turnovers all season, the fewest in the NFL
stories.summary: USA Today's Nate Davis points to Washington's ball security in Yahoo's power rankings roundup. The Commanders sit two games behind the Giants, and the win over Philadelphia was their first since Week 3. Jayden Daniels has run for only 33 yards over the last two weeks.

stories.text: Commanders host the Rams Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Los Angeles arrives 4-4 and 2-2 in its last four, with 34 points against Buffalo and 35 against Las Vegas. Washington has to contain Puka Nacua and make Matthew Stafford throw downfield. The Commanders then visit the Giants on Thursday night, Nov. 12, on Prime Video.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears pay two firsts and take the division lead

stories.text: Bears pay two first-rounders for Simmons and become division favorites
stories.summary: Chicago sent two first-round picks to Tennessee for Jeffery Simmons, and the Sun-Times column after Monday's win calls the Bears favorites to take the NFC North. The team is 0-2 in division games so far, so the standings still owe them some work. General manager Ryan Poles says the front office has been all-in since training camp.

stories.text: Two defensive tackles leave the Seattle game hurt
stories.summary: DraftKings Network lists Kentavius Street (knee) as carted off and ruled out Monday, and Grady Jarrett (groin) as leaving in the fourth quarter. Cornerback Malik Muhammad II (toe) missed the game after three limited practices, and running back Kyle Monangai (toe, thumb) has not played since Week 4. All four are listed as TBD for Tampa Bay.

stories.text: Simmons sacks Darnold on the opening drive of his debut
stories.summary: Simmons arrived from Tennessee and got to the Seahawks quarterback on Seattle's first possession. He added another tackle for loss, six tackles in all and a pass defended. Seattle ran for just 81 yards against the new-look front.

stories.text: 30: games Seattle went without losing by more than four
stories.summary: The Bears ended a streak of 30 straight Seahawks games, playoffs included, without a loss by more than four points. Chicago won 34-17 and held Seattle to 252 total yards. Sam Darnold finished 17 of 34 for 188 yards with two touchdowns and an interception.

stories.text: Bucs visit Soldier Field for Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Chicago hosts Tampa Bay on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth and Melissa Stark have the call. Watch whether the Simmons-led front can keep the pressure on after two tackles left the Seattle game hurt.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions win, then count the cost on defense

stories.text: Lions beat Minnesota but lose four defensive starters
stories.summary: Detroit left the Vikings game without Wonnum, Branch, Campbell and Reed, all of whom went down at some point on Sunday. The Lions still held on 19-15 and moved to 5-2. The depth chart on defense is the story heading to Miami.

stories.text: Rolder is done for the season, Campbell improving
stories.summary: Rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder needs surgery and is out for the year. Dan Campbell called the news on Jack Campbell encouraging but gave no medical details. Cade Mays (ankle), D.J. Reed (hip) and Jacob Saylors were not expected to practice Wednesday, and Brian Branch is in the concussion protocol.

stories.text: Vaki gives the Lions 65 yards in relief
stories.summary: Sione Vaki carried 11 times for 65 yards, a 5.9 average, when Detroit needed fresh legs in the backfield. Jahmyr Gibbs added a 30-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. Vaki's work kept the ground game moving after Saylors left with a neck injury.

stories.text: 231: Goff attempts before his first interception
stories.summary: Jared Goff had gone 231 pass attempts this season without an interception until James Pierre picked him off against Minnesota. The Vikings also sacked him three times early. Detroit leaned on the run and won anyway.

stories.text: Lions head to Miami to face the 1-6 Dolphins
stories.summary: Detroit visits Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. Miami enters at 1-6. Watch which linebackers and safeties line up for Detroit after a rough week of injuries.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Parsons set to practice as Pack head east

stories.text: Micah Parsons is slated to start practicing this week
stories.summary: Matt LaFleur said Monday that Parsons, who tore his ACL last December, should begin practicing later this week, pending medical clearance. He will start with individual drills and move to team work if there are no setbacks. The Nov. 25 game against the Rams is a possible return date, and Green Bay has its bye in Week 11.

stories.text: Rhyan out a month, Franklin and Watson hurt
stories.summary: Guard Sean Rhyan has a high ankle sprain and should miss at least a month. Linebacker Zaire Franklin has a hairline shin fracture, but the team says he will not go on injured reserve. Wide receiver Christian Watson played on after leaving the Carolina game briefly and will be evaluated through the week, per DraftKings Network, which lists a rib fracture.

stories.text: Hopper collects a sack and an interception on Young
stories.summary: Linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper had one sack and one interception in the 27-19 win over Carolina. In the second quarter he deflected a Bryce Young pass and caught it himself. Green Bay sacked Young six times in all.

stories.text: 39: rushing yards for Jacobs on 21 carries
stories.summary: Josh Jacobs found little room against Carolina, 39 yards on 21 carries, about 1.9 per attempt. He still scored twice, one rushing touchdown and one on a 4-yard catch from Jordan Love. Green Bay won through the air, with Love throwing for 288 yards.

stories.text: Packers visit the Patriots on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Green Bay plays at New England on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon called the Drake Maye-led Patriots Super Bowl-caliber on Tuesday. Parsons is not expected to play this week.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Murray's hamstring clouds the Bills game

stories.text: Vikings can't say who starts at quarterback vs. Buffalo
stories.summary: Kevin O'Connell says Kyler Murray is getting a full evaluation for hamstring soreness and the team is not at a decision point. If Murray can't go, Carson Wentz would start. O'Connell said he isn't weighing a benching, though Murray ranks 26th of 30 qualified quarterbacks in QBR through six starts.

stories.text: Darrisaw's shoulder and Jackson's quad join the list
stories.summary: Tackle Christian Darrisaw enters the week with a shoulder injury. Safety Theo Jackson left the Detroit game before halftime with a quadriceps injury, so Harrison Smith should see more early-down work. The team expects more on Murray by Thursday's practice report.

stories.text: Wentz waits in the wings with a big Week 1 on tape
stories.summary: Carson Wentz went 23 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns in relief in Week 1, when Murray left with a concussion. Murray has 1,022 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions while completing 64.1 percent of his passes. Wentz is the next man up if Murray's hamstring keeps him out.

stories.text: 0: first-quarter touchdowns for Minnesota this season
stories.summary: The Vikings have not scored a touchdown in the first quarter all year. Their offense ranks 31st in EPA per play, and their 28.9 percent three-and-out rate is the third highest in the league, according to NFL.com. Jordan Addison has two 100-yard games since 2024.

stories.text: Bills come to U.S. Bank Stadium on Monday night
stories.summary: Minnesota hosts Buffalo on Monday, Nov. 9, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. It opens a three-game stretch against the Bills, Packers and 49ers. The quarterback decision is the question to watch.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Pearce is back for Falcons in Madrid

stories.text: Pearce returns from suspension for the Madrid trip
stories.summary: Edge rusher James Pearce Jr. finishes his eight-game suspension and is set to play against the Bengals. He has not practiced with the team during the ban, so coach Kevin Stefanski said his snap count is still to be determined. With Samson Ebukam out, Pearce could carry more of the pass-rush load than planned. Pearce had 10.5 sacks as a rookie.

stories.text: Robinson Jr., Deablo and Bowman sat out in Tampa
stories.summary: Running back Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) did not play against the Bucs. Outside linebacker Yasir Abdullah is eligible to come off injured reserve, though it is unclear whether his practice window will open. Ebukam and Zachariah Branch are already out for Madrid, and Stefanski would not promise either returns quickly.

stories.text: Dotson's 76-yard catch is Atlanta's one big play
stories.summary: Receiver Jahan Dotson turned a fourth-quarter catch into a 76-yard gain against Tampa Bay. That single play made up a third of the 224 yards Atlanta gained in the shutout loss. Dotson now takes over punt return duties from the injured Branch.

stories.text: 124: pressures from the Falcons, the most in the NFL
stories.summary: Atlanta's defense had logged 124 pressures through seven games, the league high, and ranked seventh in pressure rate at 40.1 percent. The sacks have lagged behind, with 17 putting the Falcons in a tie for 12th. Pearce's return gives the front a rusher who finished third in Defensive Rookie of the Year voting last season.

stories.text: Falcons face the 5-2 Bengals in Madrid at 9:30 a.m.
stories.summary: Atlanta plays Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 8, in Madrid with a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff on NFL Network. The Falcons are 3-5 and the Bengals are 5-2. Watch how Stefanski uses Pearce and who fills the slot with Branch out; Olamide Zaccheaus is expected to take those snaps. Atlanta hosts Kansas City the week after.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers fire DC Evero, Wash steps in

stories.text: Canales fires Evero, Wash takes over the defense
stories.summary: Head coach Dave Canales fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley the day after the loss in Green Bay. Defensive line coach Todd Wash is the interim coordinator, AC Carter adds the defensive line to his outside linebacker group, and Renaldo Hill still runs the secondary. Denver will be the first game Wash directs.

stories.text: Corners and tackles keep piling up on the Panthers
stories.summary: Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson and Akayleb Evans are all on injured reserve, and Will Lee left the Packers game with a hamstring injury. Right tackle Taylor Moton came back from injury, then fractured his fibula and also went on injured reserve. Tackle Ickey Ekwonu is out and expected back in about a month, and guard Damien Lewis is missing too. Canales said the injuries played into the coaching change but did not drive it.

stories.text: Coker caught the Panthers' fourth-down touchdown
stories.summary: Receiver Jalen Coker pulled in a 26-yard touchdown from Bryce Young on fourth-and-3 with 5:37 left in Green Bay. It cut the deficit to 27-19, but the two-point try failed and Carolina turned it over on downs near midfield with 2:41 to go. Coker's score was the best moment of an offense that managed 258 total yards.

stories.text: 5 of 18: Carolina's third-down conversions at Lambeau
stories.summary: The Panthers converted five of 18 third downs against Green Bay, while the Packers hit nine of 16. Carolina's defense also gave up 288 passing yards and three touchdowns to Jordan Love, who was not sacked. Those third-down gaps shaped the loss more than the 66 rushing yards the Panthers allowed.

stories.text: Panthers host Denver at 1 p.m. ET on CBS Sunday
stories.summary: Carolina (3-4) hosts the Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Denver comes in 6-2. The Panthers have lost two straight, so watch how Wash's defense handles its first game without Evero and how the thin secondary holds up.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Nugent takes over Saints run plan vs. Browns

stories.text: Nugent runs the Saints' ground plan after Paganetti exit
stories.summary: Offensive line coach Brendan Nugent will lead run game structure this week, with running backs coach Joel Thomas still adding input on situational calls. Coach Kellen Moore called the change a workflow adjustment and praised the fired coordinator, T.J. Paganetti. Center Erik McCoy said he has not done enough to get the offense on the same page and blamed no one else.

stories.text: Shough plays hurt, Banks and Etienne stay on IR
stories.summary: Quarterback Tyler Shough has two broken bones in his left hand and also hurt his right hand after an early sack against Pittsburgh. Left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. has been on injured reserve since Week 2 after ankle surgery, with no timetable beyond later in the season. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. Linebacker Kaden Elliss is back after missing three games.

stories.text: Carlson's kicking is a problem Moore will not fix yet
stories.summary: Kicker Daniel Carlson is 8 of 12 on field goals and has missed two of 18 extra points. Moore said he does not plan to bring in other kickers this week and will see how it goes. Charlie Smyth sits on the practice squad if that changes.

stories.text: 139.4: rushing yards per game the Saints allow
stories.summary: New Orleans ranks 29th against the run and has allowed at least 100 rushing yards in every game except the one against the Giants. Pittsburgh's Jaylen Warren ran for 101 yards in Paris. The Saints also rank 28th in rushing offense at 86 yards a game, so the run game is a problem on both sides of the ball.

stories.text: Saints host 5-3 Browns at 1 p.m. ET on CBS Sunday
stories.summary: New Orleans (2-5) returns from its bye to host Cleveland on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at the Superdome. The Saints are last in the league in first-quarter points and have scored in that quarter once all season. Watch how Nugent's run plan looks and whether Shough gets time behind a line that has let him be sacked 15 times.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bowles says Bucs' passing game will be fine

stories.text: Bowles blames rain, not play-calling, for zero completions
stories.summary: Coach Todd Bowles said the weather and the game script pushed Tampa Bay away from throwing against Atlanta, calling it kind of impossible to throw early. He said he is very confident in the passing game and liked Baker Mayfield's practice week. The Bucs threw 14 passes for 64 yards across their last two wins.

stories.text: Mayfield's thumb has not been tested lately
stories.summary: Mayfield is recovering from a thumb injury, but the run-heavy approach in the last two games has not asked much of it. That changes in Chicago, where the Bucs expect to need the passing game. Receiver Emeka Egbuka missed the Atlanta game with a foot injury, and his next chance to return is the Bears game.

stories.text: Parrish leads the NFL in pass breakups
stories.summary: Cornerback Jacob Parrish had an interception, seven tackles and two passes defensed against Atlanta. He leads the league with 13 passes defensed. Zyon McCollum picked off a pass in the fourth quarter and has nine passes defensed, tied for fourth in the NFL.

stories.text: +709: Tampa Bay's rushing differential, best in the NFL
stories.summary: The Bucs have gained 1,349 rushing yards and allowed 640, a gap of 709 that leads Chicago (+467) by a wide margin. They allow 80 rushing yards a game, second best in the league, and no opposing back has hit 100 yards against them this season. On offense they lead the NFL at 168.6 rushing yards a game.

stories.text: Bucs visit 6-2 Bears on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Tampa Bay (3-5) plays at Chicago on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. The Bears are 6-2 and acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons on Oct. 29. Both teams are off the following week. Watch whether Bucky Irving keeps the ground game going and how many times Mayfield throws.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Brissett drops to third string, Love lands on IR

stories.text: Brissett falls to QB3 as Minshew takes over in Arizona
stories.summary: Jacoby Brissett went 10 of 23 for 119 yards and an interception against Dallas before Mike LaFleur pulled him, and the coach has now moved the 33-year-old to emergency duty behind Gardner Minshew and rookie Carson Beck. Brissett has 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions this season. LaFleur calls him a full part of the team, but the Nov. 10 trade deadline gives his future an obvious clock.

stories.text: Love heads to IR for at least four weeks
stories.summary: Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love goes on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain, and sources put his absence at four to five weeks. LaFleur says the injury hit a new part of the ankle, separate from the sprains Love had in each ankle earlier. The third overall pick has 268 rushing yards and one touchdown in six games.

stories.text: Minshew rescues Arizona from a 17-3 hole
stories.summary: Minshew entered in the third quarter with Arizona down 17-3 and finished 17 of 23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns. He led five scoring drives in the 33-30 overtime win at Dallas. The 30-year-old has 47 starts in 64 games for five teams and last started for Kansas City in Week 16 of last season.

stories.text: 29th: Arizona's rank in passing yards per play
stories.summary: The Cardinals average 5.44 yards per pass play, 29th in the league. They sit 18th in passing yards per game at 223.8. Minshew's job is to lift an offense that moves the ball through the air more efficiently than the raw yardage shows.

stories.text: At Seattle on Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Arizona (3-5) visits Lumen Field on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. Seattle is 4-4 and fresh off a 34-17 loss to Chicago, its first double-digit defeat in nearly two years. Watch Minshew in his first start since last December against a Seahawks team that wants to fix its offense.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Stafford gets rid of the ball fast to beat pressure

stories.text: Stafford's quick release answers the Rams' early pressure
stories.summary: Matthew Stafford averaged 2.38 seconds to throw against the Chargers, his third-quickest game since joining the Rams in 2021. He completed 13 of 14 quick passes for 94 yards and a touchdown. Chargers pressure hit him on 5 of his first 11 dropbacks, then on just 1 of his last 15, and Los Angeles won 24-9.

stories.text: Garrett's 21-day window opens, Coleman waits
stories.summary: Myles Garrett returns to practice this week, which starts his 21-day clock after knee surgery, and Sean McVay will not set expectations for Sunday. Garrett has 125.5 career sacks. Washington left tackle Brandon Coleman would face him if he plays. Tight end Terrance Ferguson, out since a Week 3 ankle sprain, is more likely than not to open his practice window too.

stories.text: Corum is the Rams' hot back
stories.summary: Blake Corum ran 11 times for 73 yards and a 23-yard third-quarter touchdown against the Chargers. His 6.6 yards per carry included 5.8 after contact, his best mark of the season. Coverage of the game says he has looked like the better back than Kyren Williams the past two weeks.

stories.text: 369: Nacua's catches through 50 games
stories.summary: Puka Nacua has 369 receptions through 50 career games. That is 23 more than any other player in NFL history through the same span, per NFL Research. Eleven of Stafford's 17 completions went to Nacua against the Chargers.

stories.text: At Washington on Sunday, 1:00 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Rams (4-4) travel to Washington on Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on Fox. They started 2-4 and have won two straight, over the Raiders and Chargers. Watch Garrett's status and whether Stafford tops 200 passing yards after two straight weeks below it.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Buckner is back as the Niners fix their line

stories.text: 49ers reacquire DeForest Buckner
stories.summary: San Francisco brought back three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to bolster its front. Yahoo Sports reports the trade came from the Colts, and terms have not been disclosed. The move arrives as the 49ers (6-1) return from the bye with the NFC West lead.

stories.text: McCaffrey's hamstring strain is mild, Shanahan says
stories.summary: Christian McCaffrey left the Falcons game with what the team first called a thigh injury, then came back in the second half. Kyle Shanahan later described it as a mild hamstring strain and said the team is pretty optimistic he plays against the Raiders. The bye gave him extra time to heal.

stories.text: Purdy needs protection after seven sacks
stories.summary: Brock Purdy took no sacks in San Francisco's first four games, then went down seven times in the three games before the bye. His last outing was a 288-yard day with one touchdown and two interceptions in the loss to Atlanta. The returning line and receivers will decide if he gets back to early-season form.

stories.text: 4: turnovers in the Niners' only loss
stories.summary: San Francisco turned the ball over four times in its 29-20 loss to Atlanta in Week 7, the only blemish on a 6-1 record. Purdy threw two of the interceptions.

stories.text: Raiders at Levi's on Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: The 49ers host the Raiders on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. Las Vegas is 4-4 after a 38-33 win over the Jets. Kirk Cousins threw three touchdowns in that game and Brock Bowers caught seven passes for 92 yards and two scores, so the 49ers secondary has a clear job.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: New-look line and Darnold turnovers sink Seattle

stories.text: Seahawks' line shuffle struggles in its first test
stories.summary: Seattle traded for guard Quenton Nelson, then played Monday without left tackle Charles Cross and moved three linemen into new spots. Grey Zabel started at right guard for the first time as a pro. Chicago won 34-17, and the line played a part in an offense that managed 252 yards.

stories.text: Cross and Shaheed remain on the sideline
stories.summary: Left tackle Charles Cross missed the Bears game with an ankle sprain. Receiver Rashid Shaheed was ruled out with a knee injury, and Mike Macdonald said the team would reassess him this week. Running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned, and linebacker Drake Thomas came back from an ankle injury.

stories.text: Darnold's turnover habit follows him to Monday
stories.summary: Sam Darnold finished 17 of 34 for 188 yards, two touchdowns and an interception against Chicago. He has 10 touchdown passes and nine interceptions this season, and his 29 turnovers since the start of last year lead the league. He said Seattle had chances to get the ball out quickly and did not.

stories.text: 30: straight games without losing by more than four
stories.summary: Seattle had gone 30 straight games without losing by more than four points before Chicago won by 17. The Bears win was the Seahawks' first double-digit loss in nearly two years. The Seahawks had beaten Kansas City 20-3 the week before.

stories.text: Cardinals at Lumen Field Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Seattle (4-4) hosts Arizona (3-5) on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on Fox. The Seahawks gave up 34 points to Chicago and went 1 of 11 on third down. Macdonald says the need to improve is high, and the Cardinals arrive with a new starting quarterback in Gardner Minshew.
